reproduction_target: ICE (Iterative/Imputation-based Cell Enrichment): an R package that detects cells enriched for a weakly/sparsely expressed gene set in scRNA-seq. Pipeline: (1) MAGIC imputation of the single-cell expression matrix; (2) per-cell single-sample GSEA enrichment scores over a predefined gene set (via GSVA); (3) derivative-based cutoff on the sorted ES curve (pracma v2.4.4); (4) iterative marker refinement using Seurat differential-expression top-n markers. Claimed results include raising senescence-detection precision in pancreatic alpha cells from 56% to 98%, identifying senescent muscle FAPs, and marker-specific populations (CDKN1A/p21, CDKN2A/p16, ATF3, MX1) in aging beta cells and AD microglia. Benchmarked against GSEA, GSVA, zscore, PLAGE, UCell, AUCell on public datasets (pancreas GSE84133, stressed beta cells GSE114297, PsychENCODE brain, AD microglia syn52293417).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-computational-stage from Methods prose + GitHub README (github.com/pxulab/ICE) read at prose level only (stage-1); no workflow/package source read line-by-line. Pure-computational tool paper; no wet-lab (W=0). Assessment targets bioRxiv v1 (canonical DOI). Note: a later published version (Genome Biology 2026, doi:10.1186/s13059-026-03997-0) additionally archives source on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.18426273) as a release_snapshot, but v1's code/data-availability statement cites only the floating GitHub repo, so v1 capture is 'floating'.

steps.label: Input loading & normalization (Seurat): public scRNA-seq datasets (pancreas GSE84133; stressed beta GSE114297; PsychENCODE brain; AD microglia syn52293417) plus a shipped example matrix (pancreas_normalized.RDS) and gene set (input_gene_set.tsv) in the ICE package; normalized gene-by-cell matrix used as ICE input

MAGIC imputation of the single-cell matrix (magic-impute via reticulate/Rmagic): kNN graph on Euclidean distance, Gaussian-kernel affinity, diffusion smoothing to impute dropout; MAGIC parameters described qualitatively (no exact k/t/decay values in prose)
Per-cell enrichment scoring: single-sample GSEA over the predefined gene set (GSVA package), running-sum on per-cell ranked expression producing an ES matrix

Derivative-based cutoff estimation (pracma v2.4.4): sort ES descending, compute forward differences, take cutoff from the initial peak in the derivative trend to separate enriched vs non-enriched cells

Iterative marker refinement (Seurat): differential-expression on the initial cell classification, take top-n positive markers to replace the input marker list, recompute ES + cutoff iteratively; n is a user-tunable variable
Benchmarking against alternative scoring methods: GSEA, GSVA, zscore, PLAGE (bulk-based) and UCell, AUCell (single-cell-based) compared to ICE on the benchmark datasets

headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on the 5 core ICE-pipeline steps (C1-C5): the ICE R package is public (github.com/pxulab/ICE, MIT, R), the README documents a conda + R install path, and the core datasets are public (GEO GSE84133/GSE114297) with a shipped example matrix. Environment is 'floating': the conda env pins only python=3.10, magic-impute is installed unpinned, and R deps (Seurat, GSVA, pracma, Rmagic, ICE) are installed via install.packages/BiocManager/devtools::install_github HEAD with no environment.yml/renv.lock/conda-lock/container. Only one exact prose pin exists (pracma v2.4.4, C4). Because capture is 'floating' (not exact_pins_partial/release_snapshot/env_lock/container), even a perfect stage2 run could not exceed RI — NOT a stage2 R★ candidate. C6 (benchmark comparison methods) is NI: the six alternative scoring tools are not part of the ICE install instructions and carry no version or parameter specification in prose.
headline.coverage: 6 computational steps assessed from Methods prose + GitHub README (prose only). No wet-lab steps (W=0).

gaps.where: Software environment (GitHub README install instructions + Methods)
gaps.missing: No environment.yml / renv.lock / conda-lock / container. The documented conda env pins only python=3.10; magic-impute is installed unpinned (conda -c conda-forge -c bioconda), and R packages (dplyr, pracma, Seurat, GSVA, reticulate, Rmagic, ICE) are installed via install.packages/BiocManager/devtools::install_github at HEAD. The only exact version stated anywhere is pracma v2.4.4 (in Methods prose). A Linux LD_PRELOAD libstdc++ workaround is noted, signaling platform fragility.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a renv.lock (R) + conda-lock/pixi.lock (Python) or a container digest for a declared platform, pinning MAGIC/magic-impute, Seurat, GSVA, Rmagic, reticulate, and the ICE commit; tag a release and cite the exact commit.

gaps.missing: AD microglia data is behind the Synapse database (syn52293417), which typically requires registration/controlled access; the PsychENCODE brain dataset is cited without a direct GEO/SRA accession. GEO accessions GSE84133 (pancreas) and GSE114297 (stressed beta) are openly resolvable.
gaps.how_to_close: State access conditions for Synapse/PsychENCODE data and provide a direct accession or a fetch/preprocessing script mapping each dataset to the figures it supports.

gaps.missing: The six comparison scoring methods (GSEA, GSVA, zscore, PLAGE, UCell, AUCell) are not included in the ICE repository install path and are described without versions or the exact parameters/wrapping used for the benchmark, so the head-to-head comparison figures cannot be reconstructed from prose alone.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide the benchmark driver script listing each method's package, version, and parameters, ideally in the repository.

gaps.missing: The bioRxiv v1 code-availability statement cites only the floating GitHub repo (github.com/pxulab/ICE) with no tagged release or archive DOI at preprint time. (A Zenodo archive 10.5281/zenodo.18426273 was minted later for the Genome Biology published version but is not referenced by v1.)
gaps.how_to_close: Cite a specific commit/tag and mint a Zenodo/Software Heritage snapshot referenced from the manuscript.
